title: Launch day fallback runbook and KPI simulator
summary: A practical pre-launch and day-of runbook focused on traffic scenarios, KPI simulation, and fallback decision trees. Designed to be used alongside the spike-capacity tests and the monitoring dashboard templates in the linked Confluence page.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working playbook to help product-ops, platform, and SRE coordinate launch-day actions when traffic, latency, cost, or model-quality signals deviate from expectations. It combines: (1) a short checklist for pre-launch gating, (2) three traffic scenario simulations + KPI thresholds, (3) an explicit fallback escalation tree, and (4) a compact day-of timeline with roles and communication templates.

How to use: 
- Run the KPI simulator locally (see simulation_notes) for your expected QPS and model variant mix.
- Walk the pre-launch checklist with owners assigned.
- On launch day, follow the timeline and execute fallback steps when thresholds are tripped.

Pre-launch quick checks (48–0 hours):
- Data & security: Confirm private model keys and KMS rotation completed (owner: Security).
- Capacity: Dedicated/GPU pools staged with autoscale policy verified at +30% buffer (owner: Infra).
- Telemetry: Dashboards deployed with the following panels: per-route token/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate by model, cost-per-token rolling 1h, live canary sample quality metric (owner: Observability).
- QA: 100 synthetic sessions across typical prompt lengths; capture distribution of token counts and latencies (owner: QA).
- Rollout config: Canary %s, A/B groups, fallback model mapping, and throttle policies committed in rollout config (owner: Product).
- Stakeholders: Headcount for SOC, SRE, Product-ops and CS assigned to rotation (owner: Product-ops).

Three canonical scenarios (simulate each):
1) Baseline/Expected load
- Assumptions: 1.0x forecast QPS, 70% short prompts (<64 tokens), 30% medium (>64).
- Expected KPIs: p95 latency < 250ms, error-rate < 0.2%, cost-per-1k-tokens within budget band A.
- Acceptance: green if all KPIs within thresholds for 15 continuous minutes post-rollout window.
- Action if tripped: throttle non-critical background routes, increase batch size in serving runtime to reduce unit cost (infra + runtime).

2) Sudden spike (2.5x forecast sustained > 10 minutes)
- Assumptions: organic traffic spike (marketing landing) causes 2.5x sustained QPS for 30–90 minutes.
- KPIs & thresholds:
  - p95 latency > 400ms for 5 min => warning
  - p99 latency > 800ms or error-rate > 1% => critical
- Immediate mitigations:
  - Shift non-customer heavy routes to reserve capacity (traffic routing policy) (owner: Platform Eng).
  - Activate burst GPU pool (if available) and lower model precision (quantized variant) for non-sensitive routes (owner: Dedicated).
  - If p99 latency still > 800ms after 5 min, trigger fallback to smaller, lower-latency model for interactive routes (Product + SRE).
- Customer messaging: draft status update to CS slack channel and post-mortem commitment if outage extends > 1 hour (owner: CS).

3) Model quality regression (e.g., hallucination uptick in canary sample)
- Assumptions: Canary reports 7–12% degradation on the canary prompt set or tooling evals detect a regression.
- KPIs & thresholds:
  - Quality score drop >= 8% on canary set => high priority
  - Customer complaints correlated with time window => critical
- Immediate mitigations:
  - Roll back to previous model version pinned in rollout config and divert 100% traffic to pinned version (owner: Product + Infra).
  - Pause downstream automated decisions that depend on model outputs until manual review (owner: Solutions Eng).
  - If rollback not possible, apply output filters or stricter safety heuristics.

Fallback decision tree (summary):
- Level 1 (warning): run mitigations in-place (throttling, batch tuning, enable quantized variant for background routes). Monitor for 10 minutes.
- Level 2 (severe): divert canary to pinned model, enable regional fallback, and open incident bridge. Required: SRE + Platform Eng on bridge.
- Level 3 (platform outage): bleed traffic to lowest-latency tier (e.g., hosted fallthrough model) and publish status page. Executive escalation.

Day-of-launch timeline (first 3 hours)
- T-10m: - Standup on bridge, confirm alert thresholds loaded, sanity checks (owner: Product-ops).
- T0: - Flip rollout to canary config (owner: Product). Verify 5% traffic routed and sample logs flowing to canary dashboard.
- T+15m: - Check KPIs: p95, p99, error-rate, cost-per-token. Green => proceed to widen to 25%. If any threshold tripped, execute Level 1 mitigations. (owner: Observability).
- T+45m: - Expand to 60% if green for 20m. Otherwise, pause and evaluate. (owner: Product).
- T+90m: - Full rollout if stable for 30m. If rollback occurs, run post-rollback validation tests before reattempt. (owner: Product + QA).

Communication templates
- Bridge opener (Slack): "Bridge open for Launch X. Observability link: <dashboard>. Primary SRE: @name, Product: @name, CS: @name. Rolling canary at 5% at T0."
- Incident update (if triggered): "Incident: Launch X - latency spike detected. Current p99: 920ms. Active mitigations: divert background routes to quantized variant, enabling burst pool. Next update in 10 min."

Post-launch checks (0–24 hours)
- 1 hour: Confirm rollout is stable (owner: Product).
- 6 hours: Sampling QA on 500 customer sessions across regions (owner: QA).
- 24 hours: Cost reconciliation vs forecast and document any overages (owner: Finance Ops).
- 72 hours: Convene retro to review telemetry, decisions taken, and any customer impact (owner: Product-ops).

Appendix: Minimal telemetry panels to glue in dashboards
- Per-route QPS and request size histogram
- p50/p95/p99 latency per model variant
- Error-rate trend (5m window) with top 5 error codes
- Canary quality score over time (evaluations per minute)
- Cost-per-1k-tokens grouped by model variant

Notes on simulation & local KPI 'simulator' (see simulation_notes)
- The simulator is a simple script that converts forecast QPS, prompt length distribution, and batch sizing into expected p95/p99 estimates based on empirically measured latencies per token from performance characterization. Use the script to produce a short CSV of expected KPIs across 0.5x–3x traffic scales.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize SLO wording for canary (is 15m stability window enough?)
- Add automation to promote rollback if canary quality drops by threshold automatically (owner: Platform).
- Confirm RTO commitments for Dedicated burst pools in contract (owner: Legal / Sales).

simulation_notes:
Quick simulator steps:
1) Input: expected QPS, percent short/medium/long prompts, current batch size, model variant latency-per-token numbers (empirical).
2) Multiply to get estimated tokens/sec and apply batching reductions (% latency saved per batch) to approximate p95.
3) Run for traffic multipliers [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5, 3.0].
4) Export KPI CSV and compare against kpi_csv thresholds above.
Implementation: lightweight python script lives in github.com/redwood-inference/launch-sim. Use it to pre-fill the kpi_csv scenarios before the launch war room.
day_of_launch_runbook:
Checklist (ready to paste into bridge notes):
- [ ] Bridge created and pinned (owner: Product-ops)
- [ ] Dashboards live and share link (owner: Observability)
- [ ] SRE and Platform on-call acknowledged (owner: SRE lead)
- [ ] QA sanity smoke passed (owner: QA)
- [ ] Rollout config committed and code frozen for rollout window (owner: Release Eng)
- [ ] Customer support standby & canned messages prepared (owner: CS)
- [ ] Legal and Sales on call for enterprise customers (owner: GTM)
- [ ] Post-launch retro slot scheduled (owner: Product-ops)
notes_footer:
This is a living document — update simulation assumptions and thresholds after every launch. If you change thresholds, add a short note with the rational and link to the experiment or perf-tests that motivated it.
